deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page is a working draft for Riemann's 1861 paper 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides' (Abh. Göttingen 9, 1861). It treats a homogeneous self-gravitating fluid ellipsoid with semi-axes a, b, c and a velocity field linear in the coordinates (the Dirichlet–Dedekind setting). The six quantities u, u1, v, v1, w, w1 parametrize the rotational part: in each principal plane, one combination is the angular velocity of the axes and the other is the internal vorticity. The page also uses the following symbols. Δ = sqrt((1+s/a^2)(1+s/b^2)(1+s/c^2)). ε stands for the gravitational constant times the density. σ is the pressure Lagrange multiplier that enforces abc = const. In the c-equation below the normalization abc = 1 is evidently used.

BLOCK 1 (top): planar case u = u1 = v = v1 = 0, rotation only about the c-axis.
(i) The equations are (a+b) d(w-w1)/dt + 2 (d(a+b)/dt)(w-w1) = 0 and (a-b) d(w+w1)/dt + 2 (d(a-b)/dt)(w+w1) = 0. [Mine:] multiplying by (a±b) turns each into d/dt[(a±b)^2 (w∓w1)] = 0. Hence w-w1 = C/(a+b)^2 and w+w1 = C'/(a-b)^2. These are the two Kelvin–Dedekind invariants, circulation and angular momentum.
(ii) Abbreviations: (a-b)(w+w1) = r+r1 and (a+b)(w-w1) = r-r1. Then (a-b)^2(w+w1) = k+k1 and (a+b)^2(w-w1) = k-k1, which are constants.
(iii) Equations of motion for the axes. In each, an inertial/centrifugal term appears on the left. On the right are the pressure term 2σ/a_i and the gravitational term -2επ a_i ∫_0^∞ ds/(Δ(a_i^2+s)). [Mine:] the gravitational term is the standard term -2πGρ a_i A_i with A_i = abc ∫ ds/((a_i^2+s) sqrt(Π(a_j^2+s))), since abc/sqrt(Π(a_j^2+s)) = 1/Δ. The c-equation has no rotational term.
(iv) Energy integral: a'^2 + b'^2 + c'^2 + ((w+w1)/(a-b))^2 + ((w-w1)/(a+b))^2 = 4επ ∫_0^∞ ds/Δ + Const. [Mine:] the gravitational part is consistent because d/dt ∫ds/Δ = -Σ a_i' a_i ∫ds/(Δ(a_i^2+s)), using Σ a_i'/a_i = 0. The pressure terms drop out because Σ a_i'(2σ/a_i) = 2σ d/dt log(abc) = 0.

BLOCK 2 (left middle): case u = u1 = 0, with v, v1, w, w1 nonzero, so rotation and vorticity lie in a principal plane.
(i) Four invariants: (w-w1)(a+b)^2, (w+w1)(a-b)^2, (v-v1)(a+c)^2, (v+v1)(a-c)^2 are constant.
(ii) Two algebraic conditions coming from the u-equations: b w v + c w1 v1 - 2a v w1 = 0 and b w1 v1 + c w v - 2a v1 w = 0.
(iii) The axis equations are written as a'' - τ a(a^2-b^2) = (rest), b'' - ϱ b(b^2-a^2) = (rest), and c'' - τ c(4c^2-3a^2) - ϱ c(4c^2-3b^2) = (rest). Here τ and ϱ collect the squared rotation parameters; later on the page τ = h^2/((a+b+2c)(a-b+2c)) and ϱ = g^2/((a+b+2c)(a-b-2c)). Put q = τ+ϱ and p = a^2τ + b^2ϱ.
(iv) Steady state, with the axes constant:
  a^2 τ (a^2-b^2) = 2επ ∫ a^2 ds/(Δ(a^2+s)) - 2σ
  b^2 ϱ (b^2-a^2) = 2επ ∫ b^2 ds/(Δ(b^2+s)) - 2σ.
[Mine:] subtracting the second from the first gives (a^2-b^2)(a^2τ+b^2ϱ) = 2επ ∫ (a^2-b^2) s ds/(Δ(a^2+s)(b^2+s)), as written on the page. Dividing instead by a^2 and b^2 and subtracting gives
  q = τ+ϱ = -2επ ∫ ds/(Δ(a^2+s)(b^2+s)) + 2σ/(a^2b^2)
  p = a^2τ+b^2ϱ = 2επ ∫ s ds/(Δ(a^2+s)(b^2+s)).
The struck-out alternative (τ-ϱ)(a^2-b^2) = 2επ∫(a^2+b^2+2s)ds/(Δ(a^2+s)(b^2+s)) - 2σ(a^2+b^2)/(a^2b^2) is the sum of the divided equations, and it is also correct.
(v) The c-equation in the steady state reads 4qc^2 - 3p = 2επ ∫ ds/(Δ(c^2+s)) - 2σ/c^2. Substituting q and p with abc = 1 (so that 1/(a^2b^2) = c^2) gives
  2σ(4c^4 + 1/c^2) = 2επ [∫ (3s+4c^2) ds/(Δ(a^2+s)(b^2+s)) + ∫ ds/(Δ(c^2+s))].
Eliminating σ instead, via 2σ = (q + 2επ I)/c^2 with I = ∫ds/(Δ(a^2+s)(b^2+s)), gives
  q(4c^2 + 1/c^4) = 2επ [∫ (3s - 1/c^4) ds/(Δ(a^2+s)(b^2+s)) + ∫ ds/(Δ(c^2+s))].
(vi) Bottom right: inversion of the definitions, (a^2-b^2)τ = p - b^2q and (b^2-a^2)ϱ = p - a^2q. Both are identities.

BLOCK 3 (middle and right): sum/difference variables g = u+u1, g' = u-u1, h = v+v1, h' = v-v1, k = w+w1, k' = w-w1.
(i) Product identities such as uv+u1v1 = gh+g'h'. These are correct only up to a factor 1/2.
(ii) The w-equations in these variables:
  0 = (a-b)k_t + 2(a-b)_t k + gh(a+b-2c)/2 + g'h'(a+b+2c)/2
  0 = (a+b)k'_t + 2(a+b)_t k' + gh'(a-b+2c)/2 + g'h(a-b-2c)/2.
(iii) In the steady state, combining these gives h^2(a+b-2c)(a-b-2c) = h'^2(a+b+2c)(a-b+2c). Hence h'^2/h^2 = ((a-2c)^2-b^2)/((a+2c)^2-b^2), with the analogous ratio for g'^2/g^2. Both ratios must be > 0 for real motions. This leads to the case split: 1) 2c > a+b (so also 2c > |a-b|), or 2) 2c < a+b with |a-b| > 2c.
(iv) Sign bookkeeping. From ε1ε3 = ε2ε4 and ε1ε4 = ε2ε3 one gets ε1(ε3+ε4) = ε2(ε3+ε4). So either ε1 = ε2 and ε3 = ε4 (struck out), or ε3 = -ε4 and ε1 = -ε2. A further case split in auxiliary quantities α, β, γ, δ with 2c = γ - δ is fragmentary.
(v) Fragments: an attempted evaluation of (τ/2)(a-c)(a+b+2c)(a-b+2c) + (a+c)(a+b-2c)(a-b-2c), and a side integral ∫ (ds/c^2)/(1+s/c^2)^3.

PURPOSE: derive the conservation laws, the energy integral, and the steady-state (equilibrium) conditions for Riemann ellipsoids, including the oblique case where rotation and vorticity lie in a principal plane. The reality conditions are what decide which configurations exist. All of this is material that appears in the 1861 paper.
errors: Product identities in Block 3 (uv+u1v1 = gh+g'h', etc.) omit a factor 1/2. With g = u+u1, g' = u-u1, h = v+v1, h' = v-v1 one has gh+g'h' = 2(uv+u1v1). Either a convention or a slip.

Block 1 axis equations: if the w±w1 there denote the conserved quantities and the energy integral is as written, consistency would require both rotational terms to enter with the same sign and with coefficient 1 rather than 1/2. Here a positive-definite kinetic energy gives a'' - K^2/(a-b)^3 - K'^2/(a+b)^3. The page shows -1/2 and +1/2. This may be a sign/normalization slip or a notational difference; it is uncertain from the image.
The line '(a^2-b^2)(a^2τ+b^2ϱ) = 2επ∫(a^2-b^2) s ds/...' is correct, but it is the difference (not the sum) of the two preceding equations. This is a presentational point, not an error.
The g'^2/g^2 ratio as transcribed has identical numerator and denominator, which is presumably a misreading; by analogy with h'^2/h^2 the denominator should differ, e.g. (b-2c)^2 - a^2 or similar.

results.what: Equations of motion of a homogeneous self-gravitating ellipsoid with linear internal velocity field, with gravitational terms expressed by the integrals ∫ds/(Δ(a_i^2+s))
results.modern_name: Dirichlet–Dedekind–Riemann ellipsoid equations (virial/ODE system for affine fluid motions)

results.what: Invariants (a±b)^2(w∓w1) = const in each principal plane
results.modern_name: Conservation of circulation (Kelvin) and angular momentum; Dedekind reciprocity

results.what: Energy integral a'^2+b'^2+c'^2 + rotational terms = 4επ∫ds/Δ + const
Steady-state conditions in τ, ϱ, σ, with q = τ+ϱ and p = a^2τ+b^2ϱ expressed by elliptic-type integrals; the c-axis condition after eliminating σ
results.modern_name: Equilibrium conditions of Riemann ellipsoids (types S and oblique I–III)

results.what: Reality conditions h'^2/h^2 = ((a-2c)^2-b^2)/((a+2c)^2-b^2) > 0 and the case split 2c vs a±b
results.modern_name: Existence domains of oblique Riemann ellipsoids

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of computations that appear in Riemann's published 1861 ellipsoid paper: the invariants, the energy integral, the equilibrium conditions and the case distinctions for oblique ellipsoids. Nothing goes beyond what he published.

u,u1,v,v1=symbols('u u1 v v1'); g=u+u1; gp=u-u1; h=v+v1; hp=v-v1; [expand(g*h+gp*hp-2*(u*v+u1*v1)), expand(g*h-gp*hp-2*(u*v1+u1*v)), expand(g*hp+gp*h-2*(u*v-u1*v1)), expand(-g*hp+gp*h-2*(u*v1-u1*v))]

checkable.asserts: (a^2-b^2)τ = p - b^2 q and (b^2-a^2)ϱ = p - a^2 q (both zero)
Integrand-level check that p = A + b^2 q equals s/((a^2+s)(b^2+s)) (the sigma terms cancel; constant factors 2επ and 1/Δ suppressed); result 0
The difference of the two steady equations gives (a^2-b^2)p = 2επ∫(a^2-b^2)s ds/(Δ(a^2+s)(b^2+s)) (result 0)

checkable.asserts: a_i ∂(1/Δ)/∂a_i = 1/Δ - a_i^2/((a_i^2+s)Δ). Summed with Σ a_i'/a_i = 0, this gives d/dt∫ds/Δ = -Σ a_i' a_i ∫ds/(Δ(a_i^2+s)), the energy-integral consistency (each zero)

checkable.sympy: c,s,q,p,I,J,C,sig=symbols('c s q p I J C sigma'); sol=solve([4*q*c**2-3*p-(C-2*sig/c**2), q-(-I+2*sig*c**2)],[sig,q]); simplify(sol[q]*(4*c**2+1/c**4) - (3*p + C - I/c**4))
checkable.asserts: With abc = 1 and the 2επ factors absorbed into I, J, C, eliminating σ gives q(4c^2+1/c^4) = 3p + C - I/c**4, matching the page's last c-equation (result 0)
h^2(a+b-2c)(a-b-2c) = h'^2(a+b+2c)(a-b+2c) is equivalent to h'^2/h^2 = ((a-2c)^2-b^2)/((a+2c)^2-b^2) (both zero)

transcription_corrections: In the c-equilibrium line the integrand should read (3s+4c^2) ds, not (3s^2+4c^4) ds. The prefactor 2σ(4c^4 + 1/c^2) is consistent with the normalization abc = 1.
The g'^2/g^2 line as transcribed has identical numerator and denominator ((b+2c)^2-a^2); one of them must differ, probably containing (b-2c) or an analogue of the h'^2/h^2 formula.
'(a^2-b^2 s ds)' in the integrand should be read as (a^2-b^2) s ds.
The ε-sign deductions on the right read ε1ε3 = ε2ε4, ε1ε4 = ε2ε3, ε1(ε3+ε4) = ε2(ε3+ε4), followed by the alternatives ε1 = ε2, ε3 = ε4 (struck) and ε1 = -ε2, ε3 = -ε4.
In the block-2 product identities the symbols are u v1, u1 v etc.; the transcription is consistent with that, but the factor 1/2 is absent on the page itself.
